gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states what each OBD tracker reports once the car is parked: Car and Driver found Bouncie reports only while the ignition is on, Automoblog found Vyncs rechecks location hourly with the car off, and Spytec's Pulse OBD manual sets a default of every 3 hours when not moving. No named reviewer has published a measured accuracy, alert delay or parked current draw for any of the three.
standout_why: I opened six of the 13 results: rottenwifi.com (cited), vyncs.com/pricing.aspx (cited), bouncie.com/pricing (cited), allinsider.net, safewise.com and hotairtag.com. None reports a measurement of its own for an OBD tracker; they give prices and update intervals while driving (Bouncie 15 s, Vyncs 60 s). None states parked behaviour. The angle itself came up nearly empty, though: named reviewers (Automoblog, Car and Driver) give only scores and observations for OBD units, with no figure in feet, seconds or mA. The parked comparison rests on a 2024 and a 2025 review plus one maker manual. Road & Track (rank 13), a Hearst sister of Car and Driver, blocked the fetch and may already carry the Bouncie ignition note.
decides: It does not decide the pick on measured performance, because no named measurement separates Bouncie, Vyncs and Spytec Pulse OBD. It does add a parked-car criterion for theft or tow scenarios: Spytec Pulse OBD (3-hour default when stationary, 2 s moving) and Vyncs (hourly recheck) keep reporting, while Bouncie was observed to stop with the ignition off. The Bouncie observation dates from March 2024 and should be rechecked on Bouncie's own support pages before the page leans on it.

findings.label: Car and Driver road-test observation (parked behaviour, signal)
findings.value: "will only report while the car ignition is on"; no signal drop seen on any of 8 trackers tested
findings.source_title: Never Lose Sight of Your Valuables; The Best GPS Trackers for 2024, Tested (Car and Driver, syndicated on Yahoo News UK)
findings.note: By Collin Morgan, Gannon Burgett and Katherine Keeler, dated 7 March 2024. Trackers were installed in a 2022 Ford Bronco with a geofence around the Ann Arbor office and a 65 mph speed alert, then driven past city buildings, underground ramps, highways and tunnels. Bouncie was the only OBD unit tested. The article reports no accuracy in feet, no alert delay in seconds and no observed update interval; the 15-second figure is from its feature list. caranddriver.com itself blocked the fetch, so this is the syndicated copy.

findings.label: Automoblog test scores
findings.value: Tracking 4.5, Ease of Use 5.0, Value 5.0, Overall 4.8 (out of 5)
findings.note: By Kristin McClure, published 5 May 2025. Each tracker was placed in the same vehicle and tracked over 24 hours on the base subscription, using an iPhone 12 Pro; Bouncie and Vyncs were run separately because the car has one OBD-II port. The article says data stops when the car is off. Accuracy is called "remarkable" with no distance given. Price at review: $90 device, $9/month.

findings.label: Automoblog test scores and parked behaviour
findings.value: Tracking 5.0, Ease of Use 5.0, Value 4.0, Overall 4.7 (out of 5); location rechecked hourly when the car is off; three-minute updates on the basic plan
findings.note: By Kristin McClure, 5 May 2025, same 24-hour same-vehicle method. No measured accuracy or alert delay. Prices at review ($79.99 device, $39.99 activation) are out of date; see the Vyncs pricing row.

findings.label: Maker price and GPS sample rate today
findings.value: $99.99 with device, renews at $99.99/year, plus one-time $45.99 activation; 60-second GPS sampling, points sent to the account together every 3 minutes; 20-second sampling upgrade is $30/year
findings.note: Maker claim, not a measurement. It reconciles Automoblog's "three minutes" with the "60 seconds" on rival pages: 60 s is the sampling rate, 3 minutes is the upload batch. First-year total: $99.99 + $45.99 = $145.98.

findings.label: Default update interval, moving and parked (maker manual)
findings.value: every 2 seconds when moving; every 3 hours when not moving
findings.source_title: User Manual - Pulse OBD Plug-In (Hapn / Spytec GPS help center)
findings.note: Maker manual, marked updated 9 November 2026; not an independent measurement. The manual lists a 115 mAh 3.7 V Li-Ion battery and 10–30 V DC operating voltage. It gives no current draw in mA.

findings.label: Maker US store price and specs today
findings.value: $14.95 per vehicle per month billed monthly, or $8.95/month on an annual plan; hardware free with either plan; 60 mAh backup battery; 8–32 V DC; 1.92 oz (55 g)
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py. Annual plan: $8.95 × 12 = $107.40 a year. The product page (60 mAh, 8–32 V) and the manual (115 mAh, 10–30 V) disagree on battery size and voltage range. No named reviewer has published a test of this model.

findings.label: Named bench test: claimed vs measured standby draw of vehicle trackers (not OBD candidates)
findings.value: Teletrac Navman Qube 300: claimed <3 mA, measured 243 mA at 10 min, 53 mA at 12 h 30 min, 12.5 mA at 13 h and at 24 h. Vodafone SCD60: claimed <5 mA, measured 3.5 mA. Vodafone SCD40: claimed <5 mA, measured 2.3 mA. AVS: claimed 85 mA, measured 85 mA at 2 h.
findings.source_title: Is your GPS tracker a battery parasite? (Vehicle Security NZ)
findings.note: By Julian, 19 May 2022, with 2025 update notes. Every tracker was powered from the same test bench and read with the same multimeter. These are hardwired New Zealand-market units, not Bouncie, Vyncs or Spytec. Useful only as evidence that a claimed standby draw can be about 4 times too low (12.5 mA measured against <3 mA claimed) and that a tracker can take 13 hours to settle.

findings.label: Cited and top rival pages contain no measurements of their own
findings.value: 0 measured accuracy, alert-delay or current-draw figures for any OBD tracker on rottenwifi.com, allinsider.net, safewise.com and hotairtag.com
findings.source_title: Best Cellular GPS Trackers in 2026: LandAirSea, Bouncie, Spytec and More (RottenWiFi)
findings.note: Also read the same day: https://allinsider.net/best-obd-gps-tracker/ (its top pick ShadowAuto is made by ShadowGPS, which the article links to), https://www.safewise.com/blog/guide-5-best-gps-vehicle-trackers/ (Kasey Tross, 11 Nov 2025) and https://hotairtag.com/tracker-subscription-costs-compared/. RottenWiFi lists Bouncie at $89.99 plus $9.65/month and Spytec OBD at $14.95 or $8.95/month, price-checked 16–18 August 2026.

unsourced: Measured parked or sleep current draw (mA) for Bouncie, Vyncs or Spytec Pulse OBD: no maker page, manual or named reviewer I opened gives one. A Logistimatics blog appeared in search with 2–5 mA for Bouncie and 2–6 mA for Vyncs, but I did not open it and the snippet cited no test, so it is left out.

Measured location accuracy (feet or metres) for any OBD tracker: Automoblog and Car and Driver give none for Bouncie or Vyncs. Automoblog's numeric accuracy figures (LandAirSea 54 within 6 ft, Tracki within 50 ft) are for battery trackers.
Measured geofence or trip-alert delay in seconds for any OBD tracker: not in Car and Driver, Automoblog, SafeWise or hotairtag.

Road & Track 'The Best Car GPS Trackers, Tested' (rank 13, 2026-04-10): roadandtrack.com blocked the fetch, a curl attempt was denied, and no syndicated copy turned up, so I could not check what it measured or whether it already states Bouncie's ignition-off behaviour.
PCMag's Bouncie review (hotairtag refers to it for crash detection): pcmag.com blocked the fetch.

Bouncie's device price and monthly fee from the maker today: bouncie.com/pricing rendered without figures ('Only 0.00 per device with 3 or more'). The $89.99 + $9.65/month figure comes only from RottenWiFi's August 2026 check.

Bouncie's current update interval and whether it still stops reporting with the ignition off: hotairtag says Bouncie's blog now claims 5 seconds and that hotairtag has not measured it; I did not open a Bouncie support page confirming either point.
SafeWise's standalone Bouncie review: the URL I tried returned a kids' GPS tracker article instead.
Spytec Pulse OBD 1-second versus 2-second update claim: Best Buy listings showed both in search snippets, not opened. Only the manual's 2-second default is sourced.

Remaining ranked results not opened within the tool budget: winchinsider.com, autoskyus.com, konnectgps.com, tagandtether.com, gpstrackerreviews.net and vyncs.com/gps-tracking-device-comparision.aspx.
